en: Having purified the body according to the *Buddhatantra-uktasiddhauṣadha-ṣaḍgraha-candamahāroṣaṇa-tantra*, one should subsequently undertake the ritual action.
The color applied to a white cloth will become excellent and radiant.
Having taken a decoction of triphalā along with one pala each of yavakṣāra and palāśa,
and having consumed it with a drink of jaggery, worms and indigestion are destroyed.
Having drunk the fresh juice of *ketakī*, oil, *hilamocī*, and rock salt,
and having smeared them [on the body], lice covered in bodily secretions are destroyed by the heat of the sun.
One should drink the fresh juice of *ketakī* with oil and rock salt (*saindhava*).
By means of the practice of wandering during the *raudra* [nakṣatra], there shall be the destruction of the *lava*.
A small amount of the juice of *hilamocī* combined with rock salt,
having been kept in the shade, becomes a destroyer of *pitta*.
One should administer the juice of *kṛṣmāṇḍa* combined with *mañcaryā* and salt;
this destroys flatulence (*cūrṇa*) and, when taken with honey, it subdues phlegm (*śleṣman*).
One should perform each [rite] for two days, and only thereafter begin the medicinal treatment;
in this way, O Dear One, it yields fruit, but otherwise it is fruitless.
One should consume the powder of *śālmalī* bark with warm gruel,
having consecrated it seven times, either in the morning or at the time of eating; doing this daily for as long as one lives increases semen and blood.
Mantra: Oṃ Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa, make this my divine nectar, hūṃ phaṭ!
Instantly [he offered] coconut and buffalo butter,
combined with the steam-mist of pork fat.
By rubbing the genitals, ears, and breasts,
as well as by massaging the entire body, they will undoubtedly increase.
Having made the threatening gesture (tarjanī) with the nail removed, and having indeed smeared [the substance] with that,
one should insert it into the middle of the womb and cause the increase of the vulva.

By massaging with the oil of buffalo butter (*māhiṣya-navanīta-taila*) prepared from *vāraṇa*, *pippalī*, *śvetā*, and *aparājitā*, there is an enlargement of the penis (*liṅga-vardhana*). By massaging with buffalo butter mixed with *śaivāla* and *kaṭurohiṇī*, there is an enlargement of the penis.

Having ground the root of *aśvagandhā* with the juice of *dhattūra* and mixed it with buffalo butter, one should let it sit for a night inside the hollow of a *dhattūra* fruit; then, after firmly massaging the penis with buffalo dung (*māhiṣya-śakṛt*), [the enlargement occurs].
Having smeared it with the previously mentioned [substance] for three nights, one should rub it;
it increases. Having prepared a mixture of *indragopa* powder and clarified butter, one should apply it inside the penis of a *māhiṣya*.
A relaxed vulva becomes firm.

One should cook lotus seeds, blue-lotus seeds, *jṛṃṇāla*, *uśīra*, and *mustaka* with sesame oil; by massaging the vulva with this, one destroys foul odors, laxity, irregularity, deficiency, and so forth. One should wash the vulva with a decoction of *nimba* bark.
One should fumigate with neem bark;
thus it becomes tender, fragrant, and endowed with qualities such as auspiciousness.
Having ground five parts of yellow orpiment, one part of *kiṃśuka* alkali, one part of barley alkali, and one part of plantain-alkali with water, [one should apply] this as an ointment to the vulva.
*Kakṣa* removes the hair of the genitals.
Then, one should rub the penis and other parts with *kaṭutaila* mixed with the powder of the tail of a *hālāhala* serpent for seven days; thus, the hair will not grow again.
By massaging with the fat and oil of a boar, an elephant, or a crab, there is an increase in the size of the breasts and other parts.
Having ground jasmine flowers with sesame seeds, one should rub it on the female organ;
it becomes swollen.
By massaging with buffalo butter, *vaca*, *kuṣṭha*, *balā*, and *nāgabalā*, the breasts increase in size.
By washing them with the water used for that [massage], they become like the penis.
One should drink the root of *daṇḍotpala* with fragrant ghee; during the fertile period, she becomes pregnant.
One should drink the root of *aśvagandha* with clarified butter; she becomes pregnant.
One should drink *valā*, *ativalā*, white *śarkarā*, sesame, and honey mixed with *mākṣika*;
she becomes pregnant.
One should drink the root of *valā* ground with water; this destroys the flow of blood.
By massaging the entire body with barley flour, cow’s urine, *sarjarasa*, and *yaṣṭimadhu* mixed with ghee, one becomes healthy.
By binding the root of *varāhakrāntā* to the ear during the menstrual period [conception is ensured].
She becomes pregnant.
By eating *kalamvī* vegetable, there is an increase in semen;
by eating sweet curd, there is an increase in semen.
One should lick amalaki powder at the evening hour with water, ghee, or honey; it promotes the eyesight, bestows youthfulness,
and generates wisdom.

One should consume *āmalakī* powder and sesame powder with ghee and honey, as well as the fruit itself. Likewise, one should consume the root of *gorakṣataṇḍula*, *aśvagandhā*, sesame, and barley, having made them into a uniform paste with jaggery (*guḍa*).
This produces youthfulness.
One should consume the powder of *arjunatvaka* with milk or other liquids. By practicing this for one year, one attains a lifespan of three hundred years.
One should drink one *pala* of *āmalakī* juice and one *karṣa* of *vākucī* in the morning; once it is digested, one should eat a meal of milk.
By drinking one kavaka (handful) of *vākucī* powder with buttermilk, water, sour gruel (*kāñjika*), or milk for one month, one attains a lifespan of five hundred years.
By doing so for six months, one becomes endowed with youth and other such qualities.
One should consume the powder of *puṇḍarīka* with ghee; after two weeks, one attains the appearance of a sixteen-year-old.
One *pala* of *śaṇa* seed powder and one *pala* of red *śāli* rice should be cooked in two *śarāvas* of milk from a cow of uniform color.
First, having reduced one *śarāva* of the milk to its essence, one should add the *śaṇa* and other ingredients and cook it therein.

Then one should consume it; once digested, one should eat with milk for three weeks, avoiding wind and sunlight. As the treatment proceeds, subsequent treatments follow; then the hair and so forth fall out.
They grow back again.
Thereafter, free from wrinkles and grey hair, one lives for five hundred years.
One should consume the root of *raktocaṭā* in the measure of a cat's paw, along with ghee and honey;
likewise, its fruit.

One should prepare a pill the size of a jujube (*udumbara*) from *āmalakī*, *harītakī*, *bhṛṅgarāja*, *pippalī*, black pepper, iron powder, honey, and sugar; then, by consuming one such pill daily for a month, one attains a lifespan of three hundred years.
One should consume one *kumārikāpala* combined with ghee and curd; by doing so for seven days, one attains a lifespan of three hundred years.
One should consume barley, sesame, *aśvagandhā*, *nāgabalā*, and black gram (*māṣa*) in double the quantity of cow dung; one becomes possessed of great strength.
One should consume one *bhadrāvalīguṇḍaka* combined with triple the amount of *harītakī* along with water and other liquids; one shall become very powerful.
Having ground the root of *eraṇḍa*, one should rub it on the head; headache will be destroyed.
One should fill the ear with the lukewarm urine of a goat or an ox mixed with rock salt (*saindhava*); this destroys ear diseases.
Alternatively, one may apply the oil of dried *markaṭa*.
One should prepare pills from *kaṭaka*, *pippalī*, *āmalakī*, *haridrā*, and *vacā* with cold water;
by applying these as a collyrium (*añjana*), all eye diseases are destroyed. Alternatively, one may apply a collyrium made of honey and *pippalī*.
One should apply an ointment of *karṇagūṭha* with honey;
this destroys night-blindness (*rātryandha*).
Having chewed *ghoṣaphala*, one should drink it with rice-water mixed with the root of *kaṅkola*.
One should administer nasal drops (nasya) into the nostrils;
this destroys jaundice (kāmalā). Having mixed lac juice, the juice of dūrvā grass, and the juice of pomegranate flowers, one should administer it as a nasal drop.

If blood flows from the nose, one should drink the root of *kāṣṭhodumbara* with rice-water; then blood will no longer flow from the mouth. By chewing the root of *sephālīkā*, the uvula (*galashuṇḍī*) is destroyed.
The root of *guñjā* destroys dental worms (*dantakīṭa*).
One should cook cow’s ghee, cow’s milk, and *karkaṭapada*;
by applying a foot-salve made from this, the grinding pain of the teeth (*dantakaṭkaṭī*) is destroyed.
By rubbing the body with a paste of radish seeds, red sandalwood, and kuṣṭha, ailments such as scabies (markaṭī) and others are destroyed.
One should drink one pala of dried deer meat with goat’s milk;
this destroys the disease of consumption (kṣayaroga).
Diarrhea is destroyed by eating buffalo curd with rice,
as well as by eating sour food.
[One should take] two parts of *kuṭaja* bark and black pepper.
One should drink one part each of jaggery and ginger with buttermilk;
this destroys *grahaṇī*.
At the improper time of day, one should consume a mixture of equal parts *āmalakī*, long pepper (*pippalī*), leadwort (*citraka*), fresh ginger, old jaggery, ghee, and honey.
It destroys asthma and cough.
Likewise, powdered *harītakī* with honey [does so].
Ginger and cumin, taken with curd or with *maṇḍa*, destroy dysuria.
One should eat equal parts of sugar and barley-alkali;
or one should drink a decoction of *śaubhāñjana* root, and the urinary calculus will fall away.
One should drink *harītakī*, *citraka*, and fresh ginger with whey (*mastu*) to destroy enlargement of the spleen.
One should eat cumin with jaggery;
fever and wind disorders will be destroyed.
One should drink alkali of barley with curd.
There is destruction of āmavāta.
One should drink the three pungents (kaṭutraya), viḍaṅga, and rock salt (saindhava) with lukewarm water.
The fire blazes up and the worms perish. One should eat *harītakī* with jaggery; the disease of hemorrhoids (*durnāma*) perishes.
One should eat *harītakī* with *śuṇṭhī*; this destroys *āmavāta*. Having ground *dūrvā* with *haridrā*, one should apply it as an ointment.
It destroys *kacchū* (scabies).

By this very [remedy], it shall destroy *dadru*, *viṣphoṭaka*, and the bites of cruel fangs and the like. One should drink the root of *kāsamardaka* ground with *kāñjika* along with jaggery and pungent oil (*kaṭutaila*).
The breath is extinguished [by this remedy].
One should consume the bark of the *arjuna* tree with ghee and other substances; this destroys pain in the heart.
One should consume *vilva* with curd and jaggery.
For the destruction of bloody diarrhea:
one should drink the juice of *mātuluṅga* with jaggery;
the colic pain will be destroyed.
One should consume jaggery with ginger to destroy all phlegmatic disorders;
one should apply *kaṭaka* with honey as an ointment to destroy eye diseases.
One should grind sour gruel (kāñjika), rock salt (saindhava), and the root of *dūrvā* grass together in a bronze vessel and apply it as an ointment; this will destroy eye pain.
One should eat jaggery with ghee, whereby wind (vāta), bile (pitta), phlegm (śleṣman), skin diseases (kuṣṭha), and other ailments are destroyed.
One should also consume the powder of the three myrobalans (triphalā) with ghee and honey.
This destroys all diseases.
One should lick the powder of *harītakī* with ghee and honey at the change of time (dusk).
Having made a dry powder of *vāsaka*, the five parts (*pañcāṅga*) [of *vāsaka*], *vacā*, *brāhmī*, and *pippalī*, one should prepare pills with rock salt (*saindhava*) and honey.
One should eat that;
wind and phlegm will be destroyed,
and one's voice will become melodious and sweet.
One should prepare pills with *vrāhmī*, *vacā*, *śuṇṭhī*, *pippalī*, *harītakī*, *vāsaka*, and *khadira* mixed with honey and consume them;
the result is likewise [efficacious].
One should chew equal parts of *yavānī*, *vūśuṇṭhī*, *harītakī*, and rock salt (*saindhava*); this destroys all types of indigestion (*ajīrṇa*).
One should drink the juice of *guḍūcī* with honey; within three months, urinary disorders (*prameha*) are destroyed.
One should drink milk with powdered long pepper (*pippalī*), ghee, and honey;
fever, heart disease, cough, and other ailments are eliminated.
One should grind the roots of *lajjālu* and *śarapuṃkhā* with tear-water and apply it as an ointment.
One should eat the root of *guḍūcī*, which destroys sinus ulcers (*nāḍīvraṇa*).
One should eat ginger with alkali of barley (*yavakṣāra*), and one will become hungry.
One should drink *jayantī* seeds with black pepper for three days;

this destroys diseases caused by sin. One should prepare a paste (*yāmanam*) from *triphalā*, *nīlikā*, black earth (*kṛṣṇamṛttikā*), *bhṛṅgarāja*, mango seeds, iron powder, and sour gruel (*kāñjika*). Then, having fumigated the hair with *guggulu*, one should rub it with that paste. Finally, having wrapped it, one should leave it for seven days.
Hair-dyeing:
Having cooked a peacock feather held in the mouth with the juice of *bhṛṅgarāja* (clitoria ternatea), one should apply it as an ointment;
hair-dyeing occurs within seven days.
One should boil one part of *pulinada* and *eraṇḍa* roots with sixteen parts of water until one part remains;
then, having strained it, one should add the powder of white *guñjā*.
After that, one should cook one *śarāva* measure of oil.
From this oil for massaging the hair, the hair is dyed.
Having powdered *bhūmividārī*, the three pungents (*trikaṭu*), and sulfur in equal parts and placed them inside a wick, one should light it.
As the wick, held downward, gradually absorbs the mustard oil, two drops of that [oil] administered as nasal drops destroy wrinkles and graying hair.

By rubbing this with *kuṣṭha* and applying it as a paste, healing occurs. Mercury weighing one *tolaka*, combined for one month with sulphur rubbed with fresh butter (*navanīta*), is placed inside a jar using a *ghaṭayantra*— the opening covered with a crucible and packed with sand— and by applying fire,
the binding of the mercury (*rasabandha*) occurs in an instant.
*Kṣaya* and so forth mean destruction.
One should take the first dung of a calf and have it made into pills (*guṭikā*). Having ground *piṇḍatagara* root, one should wrap [the pill] with it.
Having consumed one pill, one may consume poison, yet it will not take effect.
Having powdered jambu seeds, citron seeds, and śirīṣa seeds, one should cook milk-porridge with goat’s milk.
One should eat this with ghee for as long as one fortnight until hunger no longer occurs.
An ointment made of *āmalakī*, *kuṣṭha*, blue lotus (*utpala*), *māsī*, and *balā* will cause thin hair to become thick.
Having burnt *kukkuradanta* with smokeless fire and mixed it with milk and ghee, one should apply it;
even hair that has fallen out will grow back.
One should administer viḍaṅga, tagara, and kuṣṭha with wine;
this will destroy the loss of appetite.
Having taken the penis of a goat, one should tie it to the waist with a cemetery cord, or else one should tie the tail of a crow [to the waist].
Methods for the retention of semen (*śukrastambhana*):
One should bind the root of white *kokilākṣa*, or the upper part of *dhattūra*, or the root of white *sarapuṅkhā*; this is the retention of semen.
If one consumes hemp root along with betel leaf and *surasunnaka* prior to sexual intercourse, it results in the retention of semen.
Having fashioned a *karañja* [tube] and filled it with mercury, by binding it around the waist with threads, it is the best for retaining semen.
Furthermore, one should light a lamp using the oil of a pig mixed with lac-resin, *añjana*, white *arka*, and *tulavatrya*;
this is for the stabilization of semen (*śukrastambhana*).
One should cook *viṣṇukrāntā* root with flower oil;
by rubbing the soles of the feet with it, there is immobilization [of semen].
By applying a paste of white *kākajaṅghā* root and the filaments of white lotuses, there is immobilization of semen.
One should wrap the root of *viṣṇukrāntā* with a lotus leaf and tie it around the waist;
this causes the retention of semen (*śukrastambhana*).

Having ground yellow orpiment (*haritāla*), mercury (*pārada*), *rasāñjana*, long pepper (*pippalī*), rock salt (*saindhava*), costus (*kuṣṭha*), and the excrement of a pigeon (*pārāvataviṣṭā*), its application as an ointment to the penis (*liṅgodartana*) results in the retention of semen.
One should take the upward-pointing bristles of a boar, rub them, and apply them as a paste to the penis;
the penis will become erect.
Having ground the root of *kapikacchū* with the urine of a proud goat, one should smear it on the penis and produce friction; one should apply this three times.
The penis remains stiff for three days.
By washing that foot, peace is attained.
Having filled a cowrie shell with mercury, one should place it in the mouth.
One should saturate *indravāruṇī* with goat’s urine for seven days.
By rubbing [the penis] with that, it becomes rigid.
Having ground the root of *iṅgudī*, the root of *kākamācī*, and *dhattūra* seeds with camphor-water and applied it as an ointment to the penis, one may enjoy women; [the penis] flows.

Having ground together rock salt (*saindhava*), *ṭaṅkaṇa*, camphor, and *ghoṣaka* powder with honey, one should apply it as a paste to the penis; likewise, having ground pigeon dung with honey and smeared it on the penis, one may engage in sexual intercourse, and [the woman] will emit [fluid]. At the moment of union, one should have the woman eat the root of *kākamācī* with betel leaf.

Having mixed *plakṣa*, *tintilā*, and *saindhava* salt, one should smear it on one’s own thumb and index finger, insert them into her vulva, and move the channel of the Vajradhātviśvarī until she emits [fluid]. By applying a paste of camphor, *ṭaṅkaṇa*, mercury, and *hastipippalī* with honey, a woman will emit [fluid].
Having chewed the root and leaves of *rāmadūtī* and inserted them into the organ, one should engage in sexual union.

By grinding the root of *jayantī* and mixing it with rice-water, an application to the vagina at night will undoubtedly cause a barren woman to conceive. Furthermore, by grinding the seeds of *palāśa* and applying them with honey and clarified butter, or by drinking [the juice] of *raktacitra*, a barren woman will undoubtedly conceive.

One should apply the powder of *śalabha* and *pataṅga* to the vagina; it becomes firm. A skillful person should consume the leaves called *gṛhābhidhāna*, along with *śaṭhī*, *yaṣṭhimadhu*, *brāhmī*, and *māgadhī*, mixed with honey.
One should eat [the powder] with a maiden.
At the time of sleep, having made it into a small packet and placed it in the mouth, one should sleep.
By this, one becomes greatly wise.
Ghee, the root of *tagara*, and likewise the *cakrāṅkita* plant, when applied as a paste,
remove the poison caused by the bite of a venomous fang.
By drinking *samudraja-sauvīra* (antimony from the sea), poison is destroyed.
Having consecrated the wood of white oleander (*śvetakaravīra*) seven times with mantras, one should eat it; thereby, one obtains food unasked for.
In the case of eye pain, having powdered rock salt (*saindhava*) and consecrated it seven times over water, one should sprinkle it into the eyes; this removes the eye pain.

Having tied a leaf of the *kiṃśuka* tree onto a small umbrella that has arisen from the trumpeting of an elephant that has just emerged from its dung, one should cook it with clay and cow dung, dry it, and then, having made it lukewarm and adding powdered rock salt, one should empower it seven times with mantras and fill the ears with it;
this will bring about immediate relief.

At the time of childbirth, for a woman with a malpresented fetus who suffers from labor pains and other ailments, one should grind the root of *āṭarūṣa* with water devoid of living organisms and apply it as a paste to the region of the navel; she will deliver easily.

Or, for a person afflicted by a difficult foreign object (surgical obstruction), one should consecrate old ghee eight hundred times with mantras and have him drink it, and likewise smear that area; he becomes free of the foreign object at that very moment.
For indigestion, choleraic disorders (*visūcikā*), diarrhea, and colic, one should consecrate either black salt (*sauvarcala*) or rock salt (*saindhava*) seven times with mantras and consume it.
Therefore, one is freed from disease;
on that very day, one becomes healthy.

For a woman who is fertile and desirous of childbirth, one should grind the root of *aśvagandhā* with cow’s milk, stir it, and at the time of her menses, have her drink it after reciting the mantra twenty-five times. She should then approach her own husband, avoiding the wives of others.

It produces a son. With this mantra, in cases of diseases such as menorrhagia, one should grind the root of *alambuṣā* with milk, consecrate it eight hundred times, stir it into milk, and drink it; she will become healthy.
[One may also use] goat’s milk along with *abhayā*, *vyoṣa*, *pāṭhā*, *ugrā*, *śigru*, and rock salt (*saindhava*).
One should drink clarified butter prepared from Sarasvatī’s milk, consecrated seven times with mantras.
One should slowly cook one prastha of ghee in four times its quantity of goat’s milk with medicinal herbs in the measure of one pala each, using a mild fire for comfort.
By practicing for one month, one attains unsurpassed speech;
through practice for six months, one becomes Vāgīśvara himself.
A sweet voice arises, sounding like the cry of a intoxicated cuckoo;
one should not entertain doubt in this matter, for the powers of being are manifold.

At dawn, having prepared a mandala and worshipped the Blessed One according to one's means, one should drink a powder of *vrāhmī* the size of a cat’s paw, consecrated one hundred and eight times, with either clarified butter or fermented rice-gruel (*āranāla*).
Likewise, one should consecrate half a *tolaka* measure of *vacā* in the same manner and drink it for one month with clarified butter, milk, or oil;
thereby, dullness, disease, and muteness are destroyed.
Within six months, even those scriptures not previously heard become manifest to him;
he never forgets them.
He becomes a possessor of the power of retention (*śrutidhara*), with a voice as sweet as a cuckoo in rut and speech that is perfectly clear.
In the Vajravārāhī-kalpa, [the ingredients are] indrayava, vacā, kuṣṭha, tagara, and likewise mustard seed;
as well as sūṣma, elā, nāgapuṣpa, and a portion of sarjarasa.
An object fumigated with this goes quickly to sale.
O best of the wise, [use] kāleṇḍa, nirguṇḍī, and valguja;
combined with the leaf-exudate of dhattūra, musk, and sandalwood.
One who applies [this] to one's own body or to those accompanied by children shall be freed from all diseases, become free from poison, and possess a radiant luster.
[This consists of] the powder of triphalā, sandalwood, and utpala, together with śītalā.
He who drinks musk for a year shall become free from old age and disease. One should consume the powder of the three myrobalans (*triphalā*) and sandalwood together with musk;
by using it for only six months, one shall become long-lived and endowed with beauty.
Whoever constantly drinks this cool water, mixed with musk and the three myrobalans (triphalā) and kept in a stone vessel, shall become free from old age and disease.
He who constantly drinks this cool water, prepared with musk and the three myrobalans (triphalā) and kept in a stone vessel, shall become free from old age and disease.

One should prepare these twenty-five ingredients in equal parts: two types of Karavīra flowers, the two types of Candana, Kuṣṭha, the two types of Haridrā flowers, the flower of Dāruharidrā, Utpala, Padmaka-kesara, Priyaṅgu, Śatapuṣpā, white Siddhārthaka, as well as Nirguṇḍī, Bhūtakeśī, the two types of Rocanā, Trikaṭu, Vānarabīja, Manaḥśilā, Triphalā, Uśīra, Nimba leaves, the seed of Harakarañja, Hiṅgu, and Bhallātaka.

Having made this into a pill, one should employ it at sunrise, having become intent on fasting, especially on the eighth day of the dark fortnight. One should grind it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) while facing the Sun-flower (*puṣpāditya*). One should mentally recite (*japet*) the mantra of one's chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) eight thousand times. When the procedure is thus complete, one should perform the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*), the fire-oblation (*homa*), and the worship. One should apply collyrium (*añjana*) and ointment (*lepa*) to the planets and give five [applications] upon the head. Instantly, one is liberated from all defects; there is no doubt in this matter. By applying ointment to the heads of children, they shall become free from fever in the midst of the assembly.
In a dispute at the king’s gate, one should wear it on the forehead; one will be victorious.
One should smear it on the hair; one will come under the power of women.
A maiden who wears it becomes fortunate.
One should apply [this] to the navel and the birth canal of women with difficult labors; she will deliver quickly.
For all types of skin diseases (kuṣṭha), one should apply it with cow’s urine; the patient becomes healthy.
Women who cause the loss of a fetus during their fertile period should drink [it] along with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya); the embryos remain stable and they become mothers of sons.
In cases of blood-related colic, one should drink it with rice-water;
the pain will be pacified. In diseases of the eyes, one should apply it as an ointment on the head.
It destroys eye diseases.
At the time of a venomous bite, one should apply a plaster of *śleṣman*;
it destroys eye diseases.
At the time of a venomous bite, one should apply a plaster made of *śleṣman* (phlegm);
[the victim] becomes free from poison.
Pigeon dung, *indragopa*, *rasāñjana*, *guggulu*, cinnamon bark, *nakha*, *kuṣṭha*, and likewise *kanakabīja*—this incense, combined with jaggery (*guḍa*), is for all vessels.
Salep (Salābha) is the remedy for fever. Having cut balāmūla into seven pieces and tied them to the hand, one destroys fever. By tying apāmārga root, one destroys quartan fever (caturthaka-jvara).
Taking a piece of *saptaparṇa* wood, one should hold it at the base of the door on the left side;
the middle [organ] will perish.
Upon being lifted, there is liberation. Having placed the root of a *piśāca* tree in the mouth, the penis becomes functional for as long as one desires.
I do not speak otherwise.
One should cook earth-creeper with sesame oil and apply it to the sole of the foot;
that is known by the wise to cause the [limb] to remain permanently stiff at all times.

One should prepare equal parts of *pāṭhā*, *kaṭurohiṇī*, *aśvagandhā*, and *līcetanī*. Regarding the procedure, the Great Compassionate One [has said]: having ground it with the milk of an *arka* plant, a phallus (*liṅga*) should be fashioned; whatever size one desires, that shall be its size.

One should wash it quickly with warm water; it returns to its original size. Furthermore, by applying a paste of white lotus filaments, white sesame seeds, and the root of a single *navanīta* *karavīra* plant mixed with honey, the penis will not fall until that [medicine] is exhausted.
Having collected cow's urine for two nights, boil it with the products of the cow until one *prastha* remains.
Having drunk this, one should prepare the elixir (*rasāyana*) over seven days.
Thus is the excellent and supreme formulation, properly processed by Vīra.

The Five Protections (*Pañcarakṣā*): the Noble *Mahāsahasrapramardanī*, *śirīṣa* flower, *apāmārga*, agallochum (*aguru*), the fruit of *kaṭaka*, *śaileya*, *meda*, *mañjiṣṭhā*, *sukarī*, *markaṭī*, and *jayā*.
Paripelava, bala, karavīra, sāmaka, and tagara with water;
candana, āvartaka, kuṣṭha, nakhapatra, and kaṇṭavarā.
Priyaṅgu, locanā, apṛkkā, sarpa, and manaḥśilā; likewise tvac, kuṅkuma, and hiṅgu—this is the beautiful pigment when combined with the mantra.
Thus, this combined wick is the liberator from all seizing spirits;
it is likewise prescribed as an eye-salve for all afflictions caused by malevolent beings.
O Bhūta, by whomsoever the Vajra-peace is grasped with hundreds [of recitations], it releases [the affliction];
likewise, it should be smeared upon great trees and upon great caityas.
Whoever beholds that place finds no fear there from living beings;
nor is that a place for living beings, nor for those who wish one harm.
One should also smear drums, conchs, mṛdaṅgas, and paṇavas with [the paste];
as long as the fragrance of the śyāmā plant remains, the circles of spirits are terrified.
Or one may smear the wings of village-dwelling birds so that the bird becomes stuck there, whether it is heading toward its own direction or another direction.
There is no place for spirits there, nor for others who wish one harm;
one may throw [the substance] into wells, ponds, or wherever else one pleases.
For a hundred yojanas all around, there will be well-being and peace,
even amidst the falling of weapons and the encounter with enemy armies.
It should be applied to all vital points (marmans); one will emerge from it in safety.
It is also used for goiters, hemorrhoids, wounds, and carbuncles.
One who has been bitten by a snake or has drunk poison is swiftly liberated.
With this hymn, one should apply an ointment that cuts through all afflictions.
Dispute is resolved, crossing is accomplished, and liberation from the best of kings is attained;
even one who has not achieved success attains perfection, and the lord of sages attains sovereignty.
One who is sonless obtains a son; one who is destitute obtains wealth.

Soma from the *Samvarodaya*, *sillaka*, musk, medicinal paste, and yellow sandalwood—whether used individually or all together—defeat old age and death. Musk is a destroyer of disease; as a medicine, it brings about peace. It should always consist of four equal parts and be consumed daily at dawn.
With *buddhāṅgārā*, *iṣṭakā*, *kāraṇḍa*, *nirguṇḍī*, *vāta*, and *valguja*,
mixed with the leaf-exudate of *dhattūra*, musk, and sandalwood.
And by applying it to one's own body with hair from a thief,
one becomes free from all diseases, rid of poison, and endowed with splendor.
He who drinks for a year the powder of triphalā, sandalwood, and utpala, along with śitalā and musk, shall become free from old age and disease.
One should consume the powder of triphalā and sandalwood together with musk for a period of six months; by so doing, one shall become long-lived and endowed with beauty.
One who constantly drinks cool water mixed with musk and the three myrobalans (triphalā), kept in a stone vessel, shall become free from old age and disease.
If a person consumes sandalwood, the three bitter substances (trikasāya), and so forth, for six months, the desired perfection (siddhi) will arise for him; of this there is no doubt.

This is the tenth chapter of the *Mahākalparāja*, the primary source for all tantras arising from the *Saṃpuṭa*: [the description of] mercury (*sūtaka*) and sulfur (*gandhaka*), combined with *śaileya*.
Having prepared a mixture with clarified butter (*ghṛta*), one should employ it in all ritual actions.
Now I shall describe the procedure for the oil (*taila*).
Take *nalinī*-ghee, *balā*-ghee, and oil—these four in equal parts—and combine them all in equal proportions.
Add a paste of black turmeric (*asitaharidrā*) along with *balā* decoction.
Having extracted the essence of *guḍūcī* and [prepared] cow’s milk on all sides, I shall now describe the proportions for the powder:
taking two hundred palas of the powder and twice as much water, one should boil it until four *sarāvas* remain.
One should likewise prepare three parts of *balā* in three ways.

One should cook milk four times the quantity of oil, along with *guḍūcī* half that amount, and a paste made from the previously mentioned ingredients at half the quantity of the *guḍūcī*. Having combined these, one should cook them over a mild fire; if it reaches the point of burning, then move to a medium fire. Once the *guḍūcī* has moved to the surface, it is said to be "rough" (*khara*) when used for head massage; this preparation is highly beneficial after three stages of cooking.
For nasal administration (nasya), twenty palas are prescribed; for drinking, one hundred palas are taught.
For external massage (abhyaṅga), one hundred and eight [palas] should be used; thus should the well-composed yogi proceed.
For nasal administration, it may be half a thousand [karṣas], and likewise five hundred for drinking.
If one recites my words three hundred times while massaging the head, one shall become free from disease; one will possess a divine form, a beautiful voice, and become beloved;
and one will always be an expert in all the scriptures.
O you of blazing body and great splendor, the destroyer of all obstacles!
One should cook oil with these substances— vākucī, utpala, sāriva, loha-purīṣa (iron dross), gandhāśmā (sulphur), guggulu, sarjarasa, karpūra, and mṛgajoman— to increase luster and promote health.
It removes wrinkles and graying hair from the head;
it brings about the removal of all diseases—
this will certainly happen, without a doubt.
Now, the procedure for the oil for hair removal (*uddhartana*) shall be explained.
That same oil, however, [is prepared] with *raktāpahā*, *kanakadruma*, *dṛḍhaprarohā*, and *sindhuvāra*; the practitioner should prepare the water according to the previously mentioned method.
Thereafter, [he adds] *śyāmā*, *priyaṅgu*, *keśarī*, *vakula*, *vilādhārī*, *nāga*, *cakramardanī*, *niśā*, *avanika*, and *kanaka*.

Śikhī, the excellent bhūtāni, parahallabhā, muktaka, śaramañjarī, hemataru, vākucī, dhana, dāru, sarvari, mañjiṣṭhā, rogendra, nāgabalā, and white [mustard] remove all diseases. The two types of candana, mṛgamada, karpūra, śallakī, nakha-dhūpa, and jaggery, when combined, accomplish all desires and destroy itching, skin eruptions, scabies, and poison born of the body.
My word is free from doubt:
*Rajanī*, *bhava*, *rajas*, *sindhuvāra*, *vihārī*, *iṣṭakarēṇu*, *kanakapatra*, *niryāsa*, and *kastūrī*—this is considered the "Fourfold Equal" (*catussama*) formulation.
It destroys *coraka*, *utsunā*, *saha*, and various diseases such as worms, leprosy, and those arising from poison.
How much more so, then, for one who possesses both verbal restraint and the higher discipline?
